messages:
maria: Thanks everyone for coming to the security/privacy segment today. Quick thread for follow-ups and clarifications that leadership asked to track. TL;DR: SOC2 timeline, ISO ask, VPC/private deploy clarifications, audit logs retention/availability, KMS/BYOK details.

sam: Great — I'll start. SOC2 status: we have completed gap assessment and most remediation items are in flight. We still need evidence collection for Access Reviews and a couple of change control items. Target for audit readiness (internal) is end of Q2.

jordan: For the SOC2 evidence, do we have a single source of truth for tickets and artifacts?

sam: Yes — use the security-evidence repo and tag with `soc2-2026` label. If you need a checklist it's at https://confluence/redwood/security/soc2-evidence. I'll post a one-pager after this thread.

nina: ISO inquiry from legal: are we planning ISO 27001 certification or just aligning controls? Short answer: we plan to align controls first, then evaluate certification in H2 depending on Dedicated/Private demand.

alex: To add — ISO certification adds vendor audit overhead; we'll prioritize customers that explicitly ask for it.

maria: VPC / Private deployment question from product: what networking modes will be supported at GA for Redwood Private?

jordan: GA will support VPC peering and private link (cloud-provider-dependent). On-prem air-gapped is planned as a later GA feature but the early private package will support customer-managed subnets + Security Groups/NACL equivalent.

sam: Important note on audit logs: we stream control-plane audit logs to the customer's chosen destination (S3/GCS/Azure blob) and we also store a 90-day copy in our secure bucket for platform support. Customers can request longer retention as an add-on.

derek: Quick ops question — for the 90-day copy, is that encrypted with customer-managed keys or our platform key?

sam: Platform copy uses platform-managed KMS keys. Customer-managed KMS (BYOK) is supported for customer-directed log sinks and for their private deployment control plane. We'll document exact KMS scope.

ops-oncall: Also flagging: for Dedicated pools we will offer a KMS-integrated option that restricts plaintext key access to the customer's VPC. Implementation detail: HSM-backed keys via cloud KMS.

maria: On BYOK: people asked about key rotation and onboarding friction. Any frictionless flow planned?

sam: Onboarding flow will include: 1) customer provides KMS key ARN or uploads a public key (for HSM-backed BYOK) 2) our installer or console will verify permissions 3) we do a test encrypt/decrypt handshake. Rotation will be supported via key aliasing patterns and a rotate operation; customers will need to schedule rotations and we will provide a CLI helper.

jordan: Example helper snippet I'm drafting: ```sh
# verify permissions
aws kms encrypt --key-id alias/redwood-cust --plaintext fileb://hello.txt --ciphertext-blob fileb://ct.bin
```

nina: Compliance note: retention policies for audit logs must be contractually specified. If sales/CS promise 7 years, we must enable long-term archiving with egress controls and a compliance review.

alex: Action item: Sales to flag contracts that need >1 year retention. Ops/Security to prepare cost + architecture.

maria: Can someone volunteer to draft stakeholder-facing FAQ about KMS/BYOK, retention, and VPC network models? Short, non-technical.

sam: I'll draft a tech FAQ. Derek can do a customer-friendly one?

derek: Happy to. I'll slot it for EOD Tuesday.

maria: Also asked in Q&A: what happens on failure of primary region — how do audit logs and keys behave during failover?

sam: Failover behavior: control-plane failover keeps log streaming attempts to the configured sink; if sink unreachable, we buffer and retry with exponential backoff. Key availability depends on customer key location: if BYOK keys are region-scoped, we will failover to a read-only mode for key ops until keys are available in the new region (customer will need cross-region key replication or a multi-region key). We'll document recommended key setups for HA.

ops-oncall: Practically we will also surface a console banner and incident page if key access is impaired.

maria: Great. Final thing — leadership asked for a single follow-up meeting with security + product + sales to confirm comms. When can we do 30m?

alex: I can do Wednesday 10–10:30 PT.

derek: Works for me.

nina: Works for legal too.

jordan: I'll be there — will bring a short tech checklist.

sam: I'll prepare the SOC2 remediation milestone list and the KMS BYOK technical brief.

maria: Awesome. I'll book and ping the invite list. I'll also add the draft FAQ thread link when done. Thanks all :thumbsup:
